title: Gate correction denials on explicit authorship token
context: The system hardcoded human_confirmed @1 provenance for all corrections, meaning even un-interviewed agent calls could mint repo-wide denies with forged authority. This made the highest-authority write path paradoxically the least gated one—worse than hunch_record_decision, which was already tiered. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Introduce vouched flag that determines TIER, not whether write lands. Vouched (interviewed, token-bearing) corrections get human_confirmed @1 and may deny. Un-vouched (agent-recorded @0.75) corrections record immediately but cap at warning level, never denying. Authority to DENY waits for countersign; authority to RECORD does not.
consequences: Un-vouched corrections still surface at edit time and in CI, keeping Never Twice promise
Prevents forged signatures on authoritative denies—only interviewed corrections can block
Aligns correction authority model with decision authority (both now tiered)
Downstream: hunch_policy_upgrade_correction refuses un-vouched corrections (Constitution requirement)
team-matrix-e2e must now countersign blocking corrections to model real workflow
alternatives_rejected: Continue hardcoding human_confirmed (authorizes forgery, asymmetric gating)
Don't record un-vouched corrections (breaks Never Twice audit trail)
Require vouching for all writes, not just denials (loses immediate feedback)
